title: SAP Test Automation With AI Agents: How Glasslake Runs SAP Tests on Browser Use
summary: How Glasslake automates Fiori testing with Browser Use AI agents: test steps run in a cloud browser, watched live, with screenshots as evidence.
body_markdown:
**Glasslake uses Browser Use AI agents for SAP test automation in SAP S/4HANA projects. Glasslake helps teams prepare and run tests for SAP transformation projects. Its agent prepares test scenarios; Browser Use agents carry out the browser steps in SAP Fiori. Glasslake embeds a live browser view in its product and collects screenshots from the session as test evidence.**


## What is Glasslake?


[Glasslake](https://glasslake.ai/) is an agentic AI platform for SAP teams based in San Francisco. Its agent works across an SAP transformation project, from turning workshop decisions into requirements to preparing the test scenarios that validate them. In June 2026, delaware, an SAP Platinum Partner,[announced a strategic partnership](https://www.delawareconsulting.com/en-us/news/delaware-accelerates-its-end-to-end-agentic-ai-delivery-approach-through-strategic-partnership-with) with the company.


## From SAP test script to test execution


Writing a test script is only part of validating an SAP workflow. The team also has to execute every step in the target environment and document evidence of what happened. Glasslake uses Browser Use agents to carry out those browser interactions.


## How an AI agent runs an SAP test


Classic scripted test automation replays a recorded script: each step points at a specific field or button on the page. An AI browser agent works from the written test step instead. It reads the screen, decides what to click or type to complete the step, and checks the result before it moves on. In Glasslake's setup, each run follows four steps:


1. **Sign in.** The agent opens the SAP environment selected for testing and signs in with a test user.
2. **Open the app.** It finds the app named in the test step from the launchpad.
3. **Carry out the steps.** It fills in the fields and completes the transaction described in the test script.
4. **Check and record.** It checks what SAP shows back, while Glasslake captures screenshots as test evidence.


## How Glasslake uses Browser Use for SAP testing


For a test, Glasslake starts a[Browser Use Cloud agent run](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/api-v4-overview) . The agent works in a managed cloud browser, which Glasslake can watch and connect to while it works.


What that looks like in practice:


- **Instructions for SAP.** Glasslake supplies task instructions for the agent to follow in SAP, such as how to open an app from the launchpad and when a step counts as done.
- **Live in Glasslake's product.** Glasslake embeds the[live browser view](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/live-preview) in its own interface, so the consultant or key user can watch the run live inside Glasslake.
- **Evidence from the same browser.** Glasslake attaches its own client to the agent's browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol and captures screenshots as test evidence ([Playwright and CDP](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/playwright-puppeteer-selenium) ).
- **Long processes in one session.** An end-to-end SAP process can take more than a hundred actions. Follow-up runs can continue in the[same session](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/agent/sessions) , retaining the conversation and, while the browser remains active, its open pages and login.


## Working together


Glasslake's engineers share detailed session reports with the Browser Use team, with session IDs and timings, to investigate long-running SAP workflows. We work through them together in a shared Slack channel.

## Frequently asked questions


**What does Glasslake use Browser Use for?** Glasslake uses Browser Use Cloud agents to carry out the browser steps of SAP tests. The agent signs into the SAP environment selected for testing with a test user and works through the steps in a cloud browser, and Glasslake captures screenshots as test evidence.


**Why run SAP test steps through the browser interface?** These tests follow the steps a user takes in SAP. Running those steps in a real browser checks the workflow the way the user will see it.


**How do consultants follow a test and get the evidence?** Glasslake embeds the Browser Use live browser view in its product, so a consultant can watch a run as it happens. Glasslake's own client connects to the same browser and captures screenshots as test evidence.


**What is Glasslake?** Glasslake is an agentic AI platform for SAP transformation projects, based in San Francisco. Its agent prepares test scenarios from a project's requirements.


**How is an AI agent different from scripted SAP test automation?** A scripted test replays fixed steps tied to specific elements on the page. An AI agent works from the written test step, reads the screen, and decides each action as it goes. Glasslake gives the agent task instructions for SAP and collects screenshots as evidence.
